summary: An ad hoc command retrieves network device config: ansible all -i vyos.example.net, -c ansible.netcommon.network_cli -u user -k -m vyos.vyos.vyos_facts -e ansible_network_os=vyos.vyos.vyos; flags set hosts, inventory (trailing comma for a single host), connection, user, password prompt, module and extra vars.
questions: How do I get facts from a VyOS device with an ad hoc command?
What does the trailing comma in -i mean?
Do I need -k if I use ssh-agent?
How do I set ansible_python_interpreter in a virtualenv?

answer_card.title: Network ad hoc command
answer_card.answer_md:
```
ansible all -i vyos.example.net, -c ansible.netcommon.network_cli \
  -u my_vyos_user -k -m vyos.vyos.vyos_facts \
  -e ansible_network_os=vyos.vyos.vyos
```
- `-i host,` (trailing comma) targets a host directly instead of an inventory file
- `-c` connection plugin, `-u` user, `-k` prompt for password (omit with ssh-agent keys)
- In a virtualenv add `ansible_python_interpreter=/path/to/venv/bin/python`
